assumptions: The complete pinned story has no visible end marker; none is copied or invented.

The attachment reader exposed only a source reference, not the image or text. No wireframe layout, labels, interactions beyond independently sourced “Forgot password?”, or attachment acceptance marker is assumed.
For REQ-001, the wireframe is a design target only; visual comparison awaits viewable contents and does not block inventory of the independently supported recovery behavior.
For REQ-003, a test can inspect a link through the stipulated in-memory sink; the transport or format of an actual user-facing notification is not assumed.

For REQ-004–005, the same-response comparison uses requests before any limit is exceeded; the exact time-window boundary, presentation of a limited response and treatment of nonexistent-account rate limits are left open.
For REQ-008, tests use a password that the eventual application accepts; no password rules are inferred.
For REQ-009, “sign out” means preexisting active sessions cease to authorize the account; no storage, token or session scheme is inferred.

open_questions.question: What visible layout, labels or acceptance marker, if any, does the supplied wireframe contain?
open_questions.context: The image reader returned only its source reference. Assumption: assert no unseen details; compare REQ-001 only when image contents are viewable.

open_questions.question: Does “per hour” require a rolling or fixed window, and what requester-visible behavior applies when the limit is reached or the account is unknown?
open_questions.context: ACC-STD-01 does not specify boundary or treatment. Assumption: test a sixth request within an unambiguous one-hour interval; do not prescribe boundary behavior or nonexistent-account buckets.

open_questions.question: How should users receive reset links and successful-reset notifications outside the test sink?
open_questions.context: The story specifies an in-memory sink, not an external delivery channel. Assumption: inspect the sink in tests; note its production limitation.

open_questions.question: What are the password acceptance rules and active-session mechanism?
open_questions.context: The story and standard do not define them. Assumption: test with an accepted new password and the observable invalidation of existing access, not a particular policy or implementation.

requirements.statement: The application's sign-in interface conforms to the supplied sign-in wireframe to the extent its contents can be verified.
acceptance_criteria: Given the supplied image is made viewable, when a reviewer compares the implemented sign-in interface with that image, then the visible sign-in design conforms to the supplied wireframe; no particular layout, control, label or attachment marker is asserted here without seeing it.

requirements.statement: The sign-in page offers a “Forgot password?” link that starts a password-reset request.
acceptance_criteria: Given a user is at sign-in, when they activate the “Forgot password?” link, then they can initiate a password-reset request.

requirements.statement: An allowed password-reset request for a synthetic account issues a reset link usable by that account's owner.
acceptance_criteria: Given an existing synthetic account has not exhausted its request limit, when its reset request is accepted, then a reset link for that account is issued and is obtainable through the application's in-memory notification sink for testing; no email provider or delivery channel is prescribed.

requirements.statement: The response to a password-reset request is identical for an existing and a nonexistent account.
acceptance_criteria: Given otherwise comparable reset requests for a synthetic account and an unknown account that are not distinguished by an exceeded request limit, when each is submitted, then their requester-visible responses are identical, without revealing which account exists.

requirements.statement: Reset requests are limited to five per account per hour.
acceptance_criteria: Given a synthetic account has made five reset requests within a one-hour interval, when a sixth request is made within that same interval, then that additional request cannot issue another reset link for the account. The exact time-window boundary and requester-visible rate-limit behavior remain open.
Given a reset link has already completed one successful password reset, when that link is used again, then the later attempt cannot reset the password.

requirements.statement: A reset link expires 30 minutes after issuance, not 30 minutes after the reset request or first use: an unused, otherwise valid link is eligible before expiry but cannot reset the password at exactly 30 minutes after issuance or later.
acceptance_criteria: Given an unused, otherwise valid reset link issued at time T, when a reset is attempted before T + 30 minutes, then the link is eligible to reset the password; given an unused, otherwise valid link issued at time T, when a reset is attempted at exactly T + 30 minutes or later, then the link cannot reset the password. In both cases, time is measured from issuance, not from the reset request or link use.

requirements.statement: Completing a reset through a valid link changes the linked synthetic account's password to the submitted new password.
acceptance_criteria: Given an unused, unexpired link and a new password accepted by the application, when the account owner completes the reset, then the new password works for that account and the previous password no longer works. No unprovided password policy or sign-in/session implementation is specified.

requirements.statement: A successful password reset signs its account out of every active session.
acceptance_criteria: Given a synthetic account has multiple active sessions before a successful reset, when that reset completes, then none of those preexisting sessions continues to grant access as that account. The session mechanism is not prescribed.

requirements.statement: The account owner is notified after every successful password reset.
acceptance_criteria: Given a synthetic account successfully resets its password, when the reset completes, then an owner-directed reset notification is observable in the in-memory sink; repeating the flow successfully produces an owner notification for each successful reset.

requirements.statement: The application uses synthetic accounts rather than real account data.
acceptance_criteria: Given the application is run and its recovery flow exercised, when its account fixtures and data sources are inspected, then the accounts used for the flow are synthetic and no real account identities are required.

requirements.statement: The application uses an in-memory notification sink.
acceptance_criteria: Given a reset flow generates a notification, when its notification handling is exercised, then the notification can be inspected from an in-memory sink without configuring an external delivery service.

requirements.statement: The delivered application documentation identifies its production limitations.
acceptance_criteria: Given the application deliverables, when their documentation is reviewed, then production limitations of this synthetic-account, in-memory-notification implementation are stated, without representing it as production-ready.

requirements.statement: Automated tests cover the password-reset application's specified behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Given the delivered application, when its automated tests are run, then they exercise reset initiation and completion, uniform known/unknown request responses, the per-account limit, link single-use and expiry, session sign-out and owner notifications, using synthetic accounts and the in-memory sink; failures in those behaviors fail the corresponding tests.

requirements.statement: The work does not deploy the application.
acceptance_criteria: Given the delivery and its validation activities, when they are reviewed, then they have not deployed anything to an environment or service.

requirements.statement: The work does not add deployment workflows.
acceptance_criteria: Given the repository changes made to deliver the application, when those changes are reviewed, then no deployment workflow was added.
